newsitem.title: UK: JJB Sports gains after trading statement.
newsitem.headline: JJB Sports gains after trading statement.

text.p: Share in JJB sports Plc rose on Wednesday after the sportswear retailer released an upbeat statement on sales through 1996 and over the Christmas period.
The stock, a strong performer over the last 18 months with a gain of some 300 percent, was up 8-1/2p at 303-1/2 by 0809 GMT.
The company said sales in the 48 weeks ended December 29 were up 44 percent on the same period a year before, with like-for-like sales in stores open throughout the period up 12 percent.

Its sales over the important Christmas period were in line with expectations and that sales had improved across all product categories. Average gross margins had been maintained, it said, but gave no figures.
However JJB also said it had decided to close its three Spanish stores at a loss of not more than 400,000 stg.

Executive chairman David Whelan said: "I am very pleased both with the sales increases that have been achieved and particularly with the progress and development of our superstore concept, both in and out of town."
Whelan said JJB had opened 38 stores in the period including 13 relocations and had closed three stores. He said the company's store opening plan for 1997 was progressing well.
"The consistant growth in like-for-like sales and the level of sales in our new superstores is particularly pleasing and we confidently look forward to achieving further progress in 1997," he said.
